question: To visualize the morphological diversity of neuronal clusters identified through NBLAST-based hierarchical clustering, 2,143 neurons were classified by morphology and innervation pattern using NBLAST and subjected to hierarchical clustering based on similarity scores (Figure 6A); the dendrogram was cut at a height of 8 to yield 22 distinct clusters, and individual clusters of neurons are displayed side by side in the outline of the standard brain (gray), with asterisks denoting clusters of known cell types including cluster 13 (oculomotor neurons) and cluster 14 (retinal ganglion cells, RGCs).

analyse_plan.Objective: To visualize the morphological diversity of neuronal clusters identified through NBLAST-based hierarchical clustering by displaying individual clusters side by side in the standard brain outline.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: 1. Cluster Completeness: Verify that each panel shows all neurons belonging to a single cluster from Figure 6A. 2. Known Cell Type Identification: Confirm that clusters corresponding to known cell types (cluster 13: oculomotor neurons; cluster 14: RGCs) are correctly labeled with asterisks. 3. Morphological Distinction: Assess whether different clusters show visually distinct morphologies and spatial distributions. 4. Standard Brain Reference: Check that all clusters are displayed in the same standard brain outline (gray) for consistent comparison. 5. Cluster Numbering Consistency: Verify that cluster numbers match those in Figure 6A dendrogram.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Neuron Population Compilation: Assemble all 2,143 traced neurons from the dataset. 2. NBLAST Similarity Computation: Calculate pairwise morphological similarity scores using NBLAST algorithm. 3. Hierarchical Clustering: Perform hierarchical clustering based on NBLAST similarity scores. 4. Cluster Assignment: Cut the dendrogram at a height of 8 to yield 22 distinct clusters. 5. Known Cell Type Identification: Identify which clusters correspond to previously described cell types (cluster 13: oculomotor neurons; cluster 14: RGCs). 6. Individual Cluster Extraction: For each of the 22 clusters, extract all neurons belonging to that cluster. 7. Template Overlay: For each cluster, overlay its neurons on the gray surface outline of the standard brain. 8. Side-by-Side Arrangement: Arrange all 22 cluster visualizations side by side for comparative analysis. 9. Known Cluster Labeling: Mark clusters corresponding to known cell types with asterisks.

key_analysis_results: Individual clusters of neurons displayed side by side in outline of the standard brain (gray). Asterisks denote cluster of known cell types. At this cutoff, we can already see clusters identical to known cell classes (Figure 6C). Examples are cluster 13 (oculomotor neurons) and cluster 14 (RGCs).
key_analysis_conclusions: The NBLAST-based hierarchical clustering successfully recovers known neuronal cell types as distinct clusters, validating the morphological classification approach, while also revealing novel cluster identities that likely correspond to previously uncharacterized neuronal populations in the larval zebrafish brain.

summary_report.abstract: This analysis aims to visualize the morphological diversity of neuronal clusters identified through NBLAST-based hierarchical clustering by displaying individual clusters side by side in the standard brain outline, revealing the characteristic morphologies and spatial distributions of different neuronal types.
summary_report.methods: All 2,143 neurons (including mitral cells and tectal projection neurons) were classified by morphology and innervation pattern using NBLAST. Similarity scores were calculated to perform hierarchical clustering (Figures 6A and 6B; Video S5). The dendrogram was cut at a height of 8 to yield 22 distinct clusters. Individual clusters of neurons are displayed side by side in the outline of the standard brain (gray). Asterisks denote clusters of known cell types.
summary_report.results: The 22 clusters display diverse morphologies, with some showing highly localized soma positions and others more distributed patterns. Cluster 13 shows neurons concentrated in the oculomotor region, while cluster 14 contains neurons with characteristic retinal ganglion cell morphologies projecting to the tectum.
summary_report.discussion: The recovery of oculomotor neurons and RGCs as distinct clusters validates the NBLAST approach, while the remaining clusters represent candidate novel cell types awaiting further characterization.
